newsitem.title: HONG KONG: RTRS-S&P says China rating unaffected by Deng.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-S&P says China rating unaffected by Deng.

text.p: Standard and Poor's Corp said the death of China's paramount leader Deng Xiaoping will not adversely impact the BBB foreign currency rating of China.
S&P said that the passing of Deng has been widely anticipated and was considered by S&P when it assigned China a BBB foreign currency credit rating.
China's rating outlook continues to be positive, S&P said.
Speaking from New York, S&P China analyst Guido Cipriani said, "The death of Deng will complete the de facto transfer of power to Communist Party leader Jiang Zemin."

"While Jiang does not have the standing of revolutionary leaders such as Deng and Mao (Zedong), Jiang and the core leadership group have entrenched themselves over recent years. The entrenched position of the leadership group should ensure overall policy stability during the transition," said Cipriani.

Paul Coughlin, S&P managing director in Hong Kong said, "While Jiang Zemin's primacy may be vulnerable over the medium term, one should not underestimate the commitment of the leadership group to stability."

"Moreover, from a broader perspective, while there may be tensions within the Party leadership relating to personalities and policies, policy disputes generally relate to the pace of change, and generally do not reflect a desire to abondon or roll back reform," said Coughlin.
S&P said its does not believe this final stage in the transfer of power will lead to a major disruption in Chinese politics or a disruption in the continued development of the Chinese economy.
